approved_narrow_design: Treat initial preparation as an unused one-shot grant bound to the logical session, the explicit requested control mode and the originally selected PID/HWND plus normalized executable path/machine. Do not transfer the unused grant to a new process/root merely because executable and machine match.

Preserve that unused grant only when a raw connect-stage validate call fails with a typed ReadTransportError whose operation is exactly validate, actuation_possible is False, helper_retired is True, and no preparation attempt, sticky fault or possible actuation has occurred. Use structured phase/error attributes; never parse an exception string to infer safety.

Eligible verified read-only discovery/validate retries may retain the grant under the existing bounded backoff and unique target checks. Stop, identity ambiguity/change, unknown retirement, any other phase/unknown error, or any sticky fault revokes it. Never restore a consumed/revoked grant from current prepared_mode or eventual transport success.

After the same-instance unique reconnect and monitor binding succeed, run the existing initial preparation exactly once before attempting an audited native-state read that depends on its handles. Merely deleting the _outage flag reset is insufficient because prepare_mode(control) is not automatically called again after reconnect.

Consume/record preparation attempted before invoking raw.prepare_mode(control), even if it fails or raises an apparently safe validate error. Keep this attempt history independent of _prepared_mode, which is cleared during outages.

Retain the same reader, pinned job, high-water marks, live cap/target/image settings and sticky barriers. Successful preparation still gives no Save authority until all existing current-job/native AUTO/settings/CSV/sensor baseline and different-fresh-layer checks pass.

Do not change raw helper budgets, control/data audits, native Save acknowledgement, actuation ambiguity, automatic write retry or formula behavior. This is initial-bootstrap grant recovery only; existing post-preparation recovery must gain no new preparation shortcut.

Document the scope accurately: existing read_snapshot/_prepare_authorized can invoke raw.prepare_mode(control) on later matching fresh AUTO observations. This narrow change does not establish a new global no-navigation-after-recovery guarantee.
required_tests: Reproduce the old failure with a fake native-state read that refuses until initial control preparation creates audited handles. One validate timeout then same-instance retry must reach preparation once and later a valid baseline/new-layer control result without manual reconnect.

Repeated eligible validate and verified read-only discovery failures retain only the unused grant, follow existing bounded backoff, keep CSV observation running and never issue an edit/Save during failure.

No grant reuse for prepare/metadata/enter_sequence failures, helper_retired=False, actuation_possible=True, generic OSError/protocol/identity errors, ambiguous/zero/multiple targets, changed PID/HWND/path/machine, stop or sticky faults.

Consume before preparation entry; failed preparation, subsequent outages and already prepared sessions cannot renew or use the new shortcut. Existing post-preparation behavior and barriers remain unchanged.

Monitor/preview modes cannot trigger control preparation. A live cap change during initial outage survives but cannot Save the old row; original job/watermarks/settings/history are not cleared or broadened.

Deterministic first-validate read-only timeout through the real observed/resilient/session path proves same logical-session recovery with no warm-up/fresh-run reset. Retain operation/type/elapsed/recovery diagnostics.

After a new exact source commit/build, rerun the frozen-package Windows owned-fixture probe and full native/application gates. Keep both previous3/4 supplemental runs and the earlier uncertain-ack canonical failure as evidence, regardless of later success.
